content:
Apple's big September event takes place this Wednesday, when the company will unveil three brand-new iPhone models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here's what to expect.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will arrive as successors to Apple's popular 17 Pro lineup.

Rumored features include:

  • A20 Pro chip, delivering greater performance and efficiency
  • Major camera upgrade, with a variable aperture on the main lens
  • Dynamic Island reduced by 35%, for a more modern design
  • A new colour option, headlined by a bold burgundy
  • The best battery life ever, with a significant boost for the iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • Redesigned Camera Control
  • Apple's own-designed C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite features, including 5G

The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to see a starting price increase. Estimates range from $1,399, but I think it's more likely $1,199 or $1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is rumored to be the name of Apple's first foldable iPhone, with an expected price tag above $2,000 that would create a new premium market tier.

The foldable design should make the iPhone Ultra Apple's most groundbreaking model yet. It will feature a wide book-style fold, with an outer display of roughly 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches, similar to an iPad mini.

The body materials are expected to follow the iPhone Air, with a titanium frame for a sleek, modern look.

The iPhone Ultra will sport two rear cameras (main and ultrawide) plus two front-facing cameras, one for each display. It will use Touch ID instead of Face ID for authentication.

Software will be the device's biggest highlight, with iOS 27 supporting side-by-side multitasking and adaptive landscape layouts for the new form factor.

Performance should be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, also featuring the A20 Pro chip, with vapor chamber cooling and a C2 modem.

The missing members: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

Normally, we'd expect the new entry-level iPhone 18 to launch in September as well, alongside the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, this year Apple is reportedly overhauling its fall lineup significantly, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 to early 2027.

It's unclear whether this shift is purely strategic or a necessary adjustment due to the current chip shortage. Either way, without the more affordable models, this fall's new iPhone lineup will focus solely on the high-end market.

Planning to upgrade to a new iPhone this fall? Which model has caught your eye? Let us know in the comments.
